nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form. For every word $w$ over the terminals of $g$, the CYK recognizer accepts $w$ if and only if $w$ belongs to the language of $g$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the CYK recognizer

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar with initial nonterminal $S$. The CYK recognizer accepts the empty word exactly when $g$ has a production $S \to \varepsilon$, and accepts a nonempty word $w$ exactly when $S$ lies in the cell recorded for $w$ in the CYK table of $w$ up to length $|w|$.
nodes.title: The CYK recognizer

nodes.summary: Given an assignment $f$ of a cell (a finite set of nonterminals of $g$) to every word, the cell of a word $w$ built from $f$ is the set of left-hand sides of those productions of $g$ whose outputs fit $w$ with respect to $f$.
nodes.title: The CYK cell built from given cells

nodes.summary: The depth-$n$ CYK cell of a word $w$ is defined by recursion on $n$: at depth $0$ every cell is empty, and the depth-$(n + 1)$ cell of $w$ is the CYK cell of $w$ built from the depth-$n$ cells of all words. Cells are recomputed without sharing.
nodes.title: The unshared CYK recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $f$ assign a cell (a finite set of nonterminals) to every word. A production output fits a word $w$ with respect to $f$ exactly in two cases: the output is a single terminal $a$ and $w$ is the one-letter word $a$; or the output is a pair of nonterminals $B C$ and there is some $i$ with $0 < i < |w|$ such that $B$ lies in the cell of the first $i$ letters of $w$ and $C$ lies in the cell of the remaining letters.…
nodes.title: When a production output fits a word

nodes.summary: In a table listing pairs of a word and a cell, the cell recorded for a word $u$ is the cell of the first entry whose word is $u$, or the empty set if no entry has word $u$.
nodes.title: Looking up a word in a CYK table

nodes.summary: A table listing pairs $(u, X)$ of a word $u$ and a set $X$ of nonterminals of $g$ is correct when, for every entry $(u, X)$ with $u$ nonempty, $X$ consists exactly of the nonterminals $B$ such that the one-symbol form $B$ yields $u$.
nodes.title: Correct CYK tables

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form and $w$ a word. For every $l$, the CYK table of $w$ up to length $l$ is correct, and for all $j$ and $m$ with $0 < m \le l$ and $j + m \le |w|$, some entry of the table has as its word the factor of $w$ of length $m$ starting at position $j$ (positions counted from $0$).
nodes.title: Correctness of the CYK table

nodes.summary: The CYK table of a word $w$ up to length $l$ is a list of pairs of a word and a cell, defined by recursion on $l$. Up to length $0$ it is empty. The table up to length $l + 1$ is the table $t$ up to length $l$ followed by one entry for each position $i$ (counted from $0$) with $i + l + 1 \le |w|$, in increasing order of $i$: the factor $u$ of $w$ of length $l + 1$ starting at position $i$, together with the CYK…
nodes.title: The CYK table

nodes.summary: If $g$ is in Chomsky normal form, then every symbol of a sentential form that yields the empty word is a nonterminal $B$ for which $g$ has a production $B \to \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Forms yielding the empty word under Chomsky normal form

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form, let $f$ assign to each word over the terminals a finite set of nonterminals, and let $w$ be a nonempty word. For $0 < i < |w|$ write $u_i$ for the prefix of $w$ of length $i$ and $v_i$ for the remaining suffix, so that $w = u_i v_i$. Suppose that for every such $i$ and every nonterminal $B$, $B \in f(u_i)$ if and only if $B$ yields $u_i$, and $B \in f(v_i)$…
nodes.title: The CYK step

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form. For every natural number $n$, every nonterminal $A$ and every nonempty word $w$ of length at most $n$, $A$ lies in the depth-$n$ CYK cell of $w$ if and only if $A$ yields $w$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the CYK recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form. If a nonterminal $B$ occurs in the output of some production of $g$, then $g$ has no production $B \to \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Nonterminals in outputs have no empty production

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form, $A$ a nonterminal and $w$ a nonempty word. Then $A$ yields $w$ if and only if $g$ has a production $A \to a$ with $a$ a terminal and $w = a$, or a production $A \to BC$ with nonterminals $B$ and $C$ and nonempty words $w_1$ and $w_2$ such that $w = w_1 w_2$, $B$ yields $w_1$ and $C$ yields $w_2$.
nodes.title: Shape of yields under Chomsky normal form

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
